claim.anchor: Asbestos Hills, Northern Cape, South Africa — crocidolite-bearing banded iron formation; Gutzmer-Beukes-Cairncross surficial-alteration interpretation
claim.description: Execute the Gutzmer, Beukes & Cairncross (2004) field model: an older metamorphic crocidolite seam is exposed to near-surface silicification and oxidation. Tiger's eye can form only after the mass ledger accepts oxidative crocidolite loss.

deterministic.reason: Miyano and Klein's metamorphosed-iron-formation stability field permits crocidolite-to-amosite competition before exposure.
An Fe-carbonate precursor/accessory is compatible with the older metamorphic BIF seam.
Silica deposition accompanies the older seam and subsequent silicification, but is subordinate to the tiger's-eye replacement contract.
A supported Fe-oxyhydroxide product of the authored near-surface oxidative alteration stage.
Hydrated silica is a plausible transient competitor during low-temperature surficial silicification.
A minor Fe-oxyhydroxide competitor is plausible in the late vadose oxidation window, subordinate to hematite/goethite.

sources: Gutzmer J., Beukes N.J. & Cairncross B. (2004) — New interpretation of the origin of tiger's-eye: Comment. Geology 32(1):e44. DOI 10.1130/0091-7613-32.1.e44. Field transition from tiger's-eye through hawk's-eye to crocidolite and restriction to the shallow silicified/goethitized zone.

Miyano T. & Klein C. (1983) — Evaluation of the Stability Relations of Amphibole Asbestos in Metamorphosed Iron-Formations. Mining Geology 33:213-222. DOI 10.11456/shigenchishitsu1951.33.213. Crocidolite/amosite stability and BIF assemblages at 150-450°C.
notes: This paired scenario executes the field interpretation in Gutzmer, Beukes & Cairncross (2004, Geology 32:e44): tiger's-eye is restricted to a shallow silicified/goethitized planation surface and grades downward through hawk's-eye to unaltered crocidolite. They argue for later alteration of older crocidolite and state that the result is not a pseudomorph sensu stricto.

The initial 300°C stage grows the older BIF amphibole-asbestos seam inside the Miyano & Klein (1983) stability family. At step 58, a silica-rich oxidizing surface boundary arrives; the nucleator remains locked until a negative oxidative crocidolite zone is actually accepted by the mass-balanced growth transaction.

The simulated 40-60°C surface values are transparent process proxies. The paper constrains field depth relationships, not a unique temperature-pressure path; pressure 1.0 kbar belongs only to the precursor metamorphic stage, and the event explicitly resets fluid and rock pressure to the simulator's 0.001 kbar atmospheric floor.
Shape seed 2004 is authored independently from gameplay seed 42 and records the publication year of the modeled comment.
